claim: Linear generates every theme from 3 inputs (base color, accent color, contrast) in LCH instead of 98 hand-set variables; LCH keeps perceived lightness equal across hues so status colors at equal lightness read equally bright on dark.
verbatim_quote: instead of having to define 98 specific variables for each theme, we defined three: base color, accent color, and contrast... LCH has the benefit that it's perpetually uniform, meaning a red and a yellow color with lightness 50 will appear roughly equally light

claim: Linear deliberately limited how much of its brand blue went into neutral color calculations to get 'a more neutral and timeless appearance', and raised content contrast (text/neutral icons lighter in dark mode) — chrome calm, content loud.
verbatim_quote: The latter was achieved by limiting how much chrome (blue in our case) was used in the calculations applied to our color system. The contrast of the content has also been improved by making our text and neutral icons darker in light mode and lighter in dark mode.

claim: Vercel Geist maps a 10-step gray scale to fixed roles: steps 1-3 component backgrounds (default/hover/active — badges may use 2-3), steps 4-6 borders (default/hover/active), steps 7-8 high-contrast backgrounds, steps 9-10 secondary/primary text.
verbatim_quote: Color 1 Default background / Color 2 Hover background / Color 3 Active background... Color 4 Default border / Color 5 Hover border / Color 6 Active border... Color 9 Secondary text and icons / Color 10 Primary text and icons
quote: Color 1 Default background / Color 2 Hover background / Color 3 Active background... Color 4 Default border / Color 5 Hover border / Color 6 Active border... Color 9 Secondary text and icons / Color 10 Primary text and icons

claim: Geist border discipline: use solid gray for borders by default, gray-alpha only when edge must blend (shadows/overlays); keep dividers inside borders — overlapping alpha borders create visible hotspots; keep shadows translucent (opaque shadows leave gray halo on dark).
verbatim_quote: Use solid gray by default. Use the matching gray-alpha step only when the edge needs to blend with its surface... Do Keep the divider inside the border... Avoid Overlapping alpha borders make intersections stand out... Avoid Opaque shadows leave a gray halo.

claim: Material dark contrast rule: surface must be dark enough that white text hits ≥15.8:1 on the BASE surface, guaranteeing ≥4.5:1 AA even on the lightest elevated surface (24dp + 16% overlay).
verbatim_quote: Dark theme surfaces must be dark enough to display white text. They should use a contrast level of at least 15.8:1 between text and the background. This ensures that body text passes WCAG's AA standard of at least 4.5:1 when applied to surfaces at the highest (and lightest) elevation.

claim: Material: avoid saturated colors on dark surfaces — they fail 4.5:1 and 'produce optical vibrations against a dark background, which can induce eye strain'; use desaturated/lightened accent variants; keep color accents limited so most space stays dark.

claim: Apple HIG dark contrast floor: never below 4.5:1 foreground-to-background; strive for 7:1 for custom colors, especially small text.

claim: Apple dark-elevation model: two semantic background sets — 'base' (dimmer, recedes) for background layers and 'elevated' (brighter, advances) for foreground layers like popovers/modals; plus a 4-level text hierarchy (primary/secondary/tertiary/quaternary label colors).
verbatim_quote: the system uses two sets of background colors — called base and elevated — to enhance the perception of depth... The base colors are dimmer, making background interfaces appear to recede, and the elevated colors are brighter, making foreground interfaces appear to advance.

claim: Raycast desktop conventions for command-deck UI: no cursor:pointer on controls, no hover highlights on most controls (native desktop apps don't), settings in a separate native window not a modal, popovers/tooltips may extend beyond window bounds; every action reachable from keyboard via action bar showing contextual shortcuts.
verbatim_quote: No `cursor: pointer` on interactive controls. Desktop apps don't do this... No hover highlights on most controls. On macOS, buttons and list items don't highlight on hover the way they do on the web. Settings open in a separate native window, not a modal or a side panel.

claim: Raycast command-deck anatomy: big search bar at top ('almost every interaction goes through it'), uniform-height list rows with a leading icon for scan speed, and a bottom action bar — left side navigation title + toast, right side contextual actions with keyboard shortcuts; design principles 'fast, simple, delightful'.
verbatim_quote: The search bar is at the center of Raycast... we've simplified the user interface and consolidated actions, toasts, and navigation titles in an all-new action bar at the bottom of the window. The left part of the bar shows the navigation title of the active command and any toast... The right part of the bar shows actions available in the current context, along with their keyboard shortcut.
